verses.text: The burden of Egypt: “Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt. The idols of Egypt will tremble at his presence; and the heart of Egypt will melt within it.
I will stir up the Egyptians against the Egyptians, and they will fight everyone against his brother, and everyone against his neighbor; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.
The spirit of Egypt will fail within it. I will destroy its counsel. They will seek the idols, the charmers, those who have familiar spirits, and the wizards.
I will give over the Egyptians into the hand of a cruel lord. A fierce king will rule over them,” says the Lord, Yahweh of Armies.
The waters will fail from the sea, and the river will be wasted and become dry.
The rivers will become foul. The streams of Egypt will be diminished and dried up. The reeds and flags will wither away.
The meadows by the Nile, by the brink of the Nile, and all the sown fields of the Nile, will become dry, be driven away, and be no more.
The fishermen will lament, and all those who fish in the Nile will mourn, and those who spread nets on the waters will languish.
Moreover those who work in combed flax, and those who weave white cloth, will be confounded.
The pillars will be broken in pieces. All those who work for hire will be grieved in soul.
The princes of Zoan are utterly foolish. The counsel of the wisest counselors of Pharaoh has become stupid. How do you say to Pharaoh, “I am the son of the wise, the son of ancient kings?”
Where then are your wise men? Let them tell you now; and let them know what Yahweh of Armies has purposed concerning Egypt.
The princes of Zoan have become fools. The princes of Memphis are deceived. They have caused Egypt to go astray, who are the cornerstone of her tribes.
Yahweh has mixed a spirit of perverseness in the middle of her; and they have caused Egypt to go astray in all of its works, like a drunken man staggers in his vomit.
Neither shall there be any work for Egypt, which head or tail, palm branch or rush, may do.
In that day the Egyptians will be like women. They will tremble and fear because of the shaking of Yahweh of Armies’s hand, which he shakes over them.
The land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt. Everyone to whom mention is made of it will be afraid, because of the plans of Yahweh of Armies, which he determines against it.
In that day, there will be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan, and swear to Yahweh of Armies. One will be called “The city of destruction.”
In that day, there will be an altar to Yahweh in the middle of the land of Egypt, and a pillar to Yahweh at its border.

It will be for a sign and for a witness to Yahweh of Armies in the land of Egypt; for they will cry to Yahweh because of oppressors, and he will send them a savior and a defender, and he will deliver them.
Yahweh will be known to Egypt, and the Egyptians will know Yahweh in that day. Yes, they will worship with sacrifice and offering, and will vow a vow to Yahweh, and will perform it.
Yahweh will strike Egypt, striking and healing. They will return to Yahweh, and he will be entreated by them, and will heal them.
In that day there will be a highway out of Egypt to Assyria, and the Assyrian shall come into Egypt, and the Egyptian into Assyria; and the Egyptians will worship with the Assyrians.
In that day, Israel will be the third with Egypt and with Assyria, a blessing within the earth;
because Yahweh of Armies has blessed them, saying, “Blessed be Egypt my people, Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance.”

footnotes.content: When the Lord comes near, idols don't just topple—they *tremble*. Egypt trusted in stone and grain and the strength of the river, but the heart of Egypt will melt. This is what happens when we meet the real God: all the false certainties we've built dissolve.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When God withdraws His hand, we turn on each other. Brother against brother, city against city—this is not cruelty from God, but the fruit of a house divided against itself. It's what happens when we choose anything but the Lord as our foundation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Notice what Egypt reaches for in their panic: idols, charmers, mediums, and wizards—more broken things to grasp. When we've rejected counsel from the living God, we'll consult anything that whispers a false answer. But no spirit of darkness knows the way home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A cruel lord and fierce king: Egypt, proud and self-sufficient, will bow to tyrants. This happened in history—Assyrian campaigns in Egypt—but I see the deeper truth: those who will not submit to the gracious Lord will submit to the merciless. There is no middle ground of independence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Nile was Egypt's god, its treasury, its reason for being. But when the waters fail, everything Egypt believed would sustain them fails too. We all trust in something: wealth, health, a person, or a place. When it dries up, we discover what our faith was really in.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Reeds and flags and streams—the details matter because they ground Isaiah's prophecy in real suffering. Not abstract judgment, but fishermen grieved, fields parched, the green world withering. The Lord sees every small breaking thing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sown fields by the Nile—Egypt's harvest depends entirely on those annual waters. When they fail, abundance becomes famine, and the future becomes no more. Dependence on what we cannot control teaches us early what only the Lord can truly provide.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fishermen lamenting, nets spread on empty water—the Lord speaks in the voice of workers and their sorrow. This is not a verdict read in a palace, but a grief that touches every person whose hands know the Nile. God sees the common laborer's heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Flax workers and weavers confounded—even the finest crafts cannot survive when the land fails. Our skills, our ingenuity, our careful work: all become futile when separated from God's provision. Pride in our hands falls away when the ground beneath us shakes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pillars broken, laborers grieved—even infrastructure crumbles. Those who earned by the sweat of their brow find their work undone. Grief of soul is what remains when all we've built proves fragile, and we must finally look up.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zoan (Tanis) was Egypt's northern capital; its princes claimed descent from ancient wisdom. But Isaiah unmasks them: utterly foolish. They boast of heritage and learning, yet cannot read the handwriting on the wall. Pedigree is no substitute for knowing God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Isaiah's challenge cuts deep: "Let them tell you." What use is wisdom if it cannot discern what the Lord has purposed? The wise men of Egypt cannot read tomorrow because they've never really known the Almighty. True wisdom begins with seeing God's hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Memphis, Egypt's ancient center of power, and Zoan—both strongholds of leadership brought to foolishness. They are the cornerstone meant to hold Egypt steady, yet they stumble. When those we trust to lead us away from God, the whole house tilts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A spirit of perverseness, like drunkenness in vomit—the imagery is deliberately degrading because pride is degrading. Egypt, once master of the world, staggers in its own mess. When we resist God long enough, He lets us fall into the pit we've dug.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Head nor tail, palm nor rush—nothing Egypt can do will restore it. Not leadership, not common labor, not high nor low. This is the moment of total powerlessness, and it's the truest place a proud nation can come to: the place where only God can heal.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Egypt will tremble like women—not as insult, but as image of utter vulnerability. The mighty shaken by the Lord's hand. When we finally feel how small we are in the face of God's power, fear becomes the doorway to faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The land of Judah becomes terror to Egypt—not because Judah is strong, but because Judah's God has plans. Those who oppose the Lord's people discover He makes a way for His own. This is where judgment and mercy meet: fear prepares the heart for grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Five cities speaking Canaan's language and swearing to the Lord—the arc bends toward restoration. Those who once mocked Israel's God will speak His tongue. One city called "destruction," perhaps because it marks the breaking point where humbling becomes healing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: An altar and a pillar to Yahweh in Egypt's very heart—this would have been unthinkable before. Egypt, land of temples to false gods, becomes a place where the true God receives worship. Stones raised to Him mark a land's turning from death to life.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A sign and witness—these are the same words used for remembrance and covenant. The altar will remind Egypt of what God has done. And when oppressors come again, Egypt will cry out, and the Lord will send both Savior and Defender. This is the Lord's covenant grace in stone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Egypt will know Yahweh—not as theory, but as lived truth. From judgment came breaking, from breaking came turning, from turning comes worship offered freely. The Egyptians will vow to the Lord and perform their vows. True knowledge leads to true obedience.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Striking and healing—both the blow and the cure come from the same hand. Egypt returns to the Lord, and He is entreated by them. The door closes on judgment and opens on restoration. This is the Gospel rhythm written into history: death and resurrection, breaking and healing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A highway between Egypt and Assyria, enemies no more—both nations journeying together, worshiping together. What once was rivalry becomes fellowship. Only the Lord can make a way for nations that have fought each other to walk as one.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Israel the third—not exalted above the others, but standing with Egypt and Assyria as equals in blessing. All three nations become a blessing to the earth, a sign to all peoples of what happens when ancient enemies kneel before the same Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Blessed be Egypt my people, Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance." Readers today hear an echo of Jesus gathering all nations to Himself—old enemies reconciled, rivals becoming siblings, all equally precious to the Father's heart. This is the future breaking into history, and it still breaks into ours.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
